business_scope.primary_industry_name: Publishing of Massively Multiplayer Online Role-Playing Games

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Swiss Code of Obligations; cantonal notarial and commercial-register law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Swiss-Chinese Agreement on the Reciprocal Protection of Investments (signed 1986, in force 1987)
Switzerland-United States Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (1996, as amended by the 2009 Protocol)
Switzerland-Germany Double Taxation Agreement (1971, as amended)
EFTA Convention and EFTA Joint Free Trade Agreements (Switzerland as an EFTA State)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (Geldwäschereigesetz, GwG; SR 955.0) as amended; Swiss Criminal Code (StGB; SR 311.0) Art. 305bis and 305ter; Swiss Code of Obligations (OR; SR 220) Art. 626, 628, 697l (internal register of beneficial owners); Federal Act on the Transparency of Legal Persons and the Identification of Beneficial Owners (Bundesgesetz über die Transparenz von juristischen Personen und die Identifikation der wirtschaftlich Berechtigten, adopted 22 December 2023, entry into force pending at the time of this dossier); FINMA Circular 2023/1 on the Due Diligence Obligations of Financial Intermediaries; Swiss Commercial Register Ordinance (HRegV; SR 221.411).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of founder/UBO passport or other official identity document
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent authority or notary public in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague Contracting States)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original or certified banker's reference/letter of good standing confirming source of funds and professional integrity of each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank in the UBO's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague Contracting States)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or official extract from a foreign commercial register when a UBO is a corporate body
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry of the UBO's country of formation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague Contracting States)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Swiss certified translation into German or French of all notarized and apostilled UBO documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Court-sworn translator or accredited translation bureau in Switzerland

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of founders, UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against PEP databases (domestic and foreign PEPs), OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, EU and Swiss SECO sanctions lists, and Swiss domestic sanctions under SR 946.202 series; screening via FinSA/AMLA-compliant KYC utilities (e.g., World-Check One or equivalent); enhanced due diligence for PEP relationships, source-of-funds documentation, and written clarification records under GwG Art. 4 and FINMA Circular 2023/1.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix – Central Business Names Index (Zentraler Firmenindex) operated by the Federal Commercial Register Office at zefix.ch; filings are lodged with the competent Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory corporate names must be in Latin script and drawn from Swiss official languages (German, French, Italian, or Romansh); the legal-form designation 'Aktiengesellschaft' or the abbreviation 'AG' (equivalently 'Société Anonyme'/'SA' or 'Società Anonima'/'SA') must appear; names must be distinctive, truthful, and non-deceptive under OR Art. 950-951; foreign-language elements may be added only where recognizable as such and not misleading; principles of commercial-register naming per HRegV Art. 57-62.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Audit / Revision / Fiduciary (when implying licensed regulated services)
European (when implying an EU institutional connection)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservations and advance rulings (Vorentscheid) may be extended in writing for a further 30 days if still pending incorporation; upon rejection by the Cantonal Commercial Register Office, file a written administrative objection with the cantonal supervisory authority (Handelsregistersektion or the competent cantonal administrative tribunal) within 30 days of notification, submitting a revised name, Zefix availability evidence, and any prior-use documentation; decisions of the cantonal supervisory authority may be appealed to the Swiss Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht) within 30 days; a further appeal on questions of law lies to the Swiss Federal Supreme Court where permitted.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible for ISIC 5820 digital publishing: cantonal commercial registers accept domiciliation services from licensed registered agents with physical premises, staffed reception, and genuine mail/service capacity (e.g., in Zug, Zurich, or Geneva); purely virtual mailboxes without legal service capacity are not admitted as a statutory registered seat; for cantonal tax substance purposes (Zug and other cantons), the AG must evidence actual management decisions and operational substance beyond a letterbox arrangement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (<5% annual probability) for a low-risk MMORPG publisher with clean books and cash flows routed through Apple and Google app-store payouts; probability rises to approximately 15-20% where the registered seat is located in a high-density domiciliation cluster, bearer shares are detected, or nominee directors are used.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Advance name clearance opinion (Vorentscheid) issued by the Cantonal Commercial Register Office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal fee tariff for commercial-register pre-examinations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of bilingual (German/English) Articles of Association compliant with OR Art. 626
Notarial public deed of incorporation (öffentliche Beurkundung)

Swiss Official Gazette (SHAB) publication of incorporation
First-year registered-office / domiciliation agreement with a licensed registered agent

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille / consular legalization of three UBO identity and bank-reference documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent authorities in the country of document origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Apostille Convention fee schedule or consular fee tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified German/French translations of UBO due-diligence documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Court-sworn translator or accredited translation bureau

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP, OFAC/SECO/UN sanctions screening and UBO internal-register setup
Bank account opening and confirmation of share-capital deposit (Sichteinlage)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss bank of account (e.g., cantonal bank)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR), Arts. 620-763 (Aktiengesellschaft/Stock Company); Arts. 632-633 (minimum capital and escrow payment); Art. 640 (Commercial Register entry); Art. 627 (mandatory Articles of Association content); Swiss Civil Code (ZGB), Art. 52 (legal personality acquired upon registration).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug); federal oversight by the Federal Commercial Register Office (Eidgenössisches Amt für das Handelsregister, EAR) and the Swiss Federal Institute of Intellectual Property (IPI) for company name review.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Articles of Association (Statuten) executed by public deed (öffentliche Beurkundung) and the Application for Commercial Register Entry (Anmeldung zur Eintragung ins Handelsregister).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: CHF 100,000 minimum nominal share capital; at least 20% of the nominal value (minimum CHF 50,000) must be fully paid up before registration and deposited in an escrow account (Sperrkonto) at a FINMA-licensed Swiss bank, at the free disposal of the Board only after Commercial Register entry (Arts. 632-633 OR). Contributions in kind require a qualified auditor's confirmation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) Adoption of the Articles of Association of CH_AG, dated the date of notarization, covering the corporate object of worldwide publishing and operation of hardcore MMORPG games (ISIC 5820) with in-app purchase monetization; (2) confirmation of the subscribed share capital of CHF 100,000, with CHF 50,000 paid into the escrow account at a licensed Swiss bank and at the free disposal of the Board; (3) the registered office is established in the Canton of Zug, Switzerland; (4) appointment of [Name] as Chief Executive Officer and [Name] as Chairman of the Board, each with individual signature authority; (5) the officers are authorized to complete the Commercial Register filing, open operational bank accounts, and execute all ancillary documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Escrow deposit of minimum paid-up capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: FINMA-licensed Swiss bank (e.g., Zuger Kantonalbank, UBS Switzerland AG, PostFinance AG) acting as private financial counterparty under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (GwG/AMLA).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a capital deposit account (Sperrkonto) in the name of 'CH_AG in formation (Name in Gründung)'. Transfer at least CHF 50,000 from the founders' bank accounts. Provide originator bank statements, identity documents, and source-of-funds declarations to satisfy KYC/AML checks. Obtain the bank's Capital Deposit Confirmation Letter (Sperrkonto-Bestätigung) confirming that the funds are blocked until registration and become available to the Board upon Commercial Register entry.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association (Statuten)
Founders' passports or national ID cards
Source-of-funds declarations and bank statements
AML/KYC forms including beneficial owner declarations (Form A/B where applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines the relationship, resubmit with a corrected source-of-funds narrative or select an alternative FINMA-licensed bank. A bank guarantee issued by an authorized Swiss bank or an auditor's confirmation for in-kind contributions may substitute the cash deposit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Public notarization of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Canton of Zug (Notariat Zug) or a licensed cantonal notary authorized to execute public deeds.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founders appear in person or by notarized power of attorney before the notary. The notary reads the Statuten aloud, verifies founders' identities, confirms the subscribed capital and the named Board members, and executes the public deed (öffentliche Beurkundung). The notary then transmits the deed and accompanying documents to the Commercial Register Office together with the registration application and fee.
required_dossiers: Final Articles of Association (Statuten) text
Founders' passports or identity cards
Capital deposit confirmation letter issued by the bank (per Step 1)
List of initial Board members with identity documents and specimen signatures
Powers of attorney if founders are represented
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If formal defects are identified, the deed is corrected and re-executed; foreign documents must be apostilled or consular legalized in advance to avoid repeat notarial acts. A corrected addendum can be executed rather than a full re-notarization where permitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for entry in the Commercial Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug) - electronic filing via the official e-suite web portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Application for Entry (Anmeldung zur Eintragung) electronically, attaching the notarial deed, capital confirmation, and all declarations. The registry verifies the company name, legal form, compliance with the Code of Obligations, and the UBO declaration. Upon approval, the AG is entered into the Commercial Register and acquires legal personality (Art. 52 ZGB); the entry is contemporaneously published in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB).
required_dossiers: Notarized Statuten and public deed
Capital deposit confirmation letter or auditor's report
Beneficial owner declaration (UBO register form)
Acceptance of office declarations of Board members and the statutory auditor
Specimen signatures of all authorized signatories
Completed registration application (Anmeldung)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The registry issues a deficiency cure notice (Fristansetzung) allowing a statutory 30-day curing period to file amended documents. Priority processing (expedite fee) may shorten examination to 1-2 working days. Clerical errors in the entry are corrected by filing a formal rectification request with the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT, AHV and accident insurance registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration of Zug (Amt für Steuern), Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA/ESTV), AHV Compensation Fund of Zug (Ausgleichskasse des Kantons Zug), and Swiss National Accident Insurance Fund (Suva).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following registration, file the AG for cantonal corporate income tax and capital tax with the Zug tax administration; register for federal VAT through the FTA online portal (mandatory once worldwide turnover from MMORPG in-app purchases exceeds CHF 100,000 annually); enroll as an employer with the AHV compensation fund for social security contributions; and register for mandatory accident insurance (UVG/LAA) with Suva, including the occupational risk tariff declaration.
required_dossiers: Certified Commercial Register extract (Handelsregisterauszug)
Federal VAT registration form (FTA online)
Cantonal tax registration questionnaire and opening balance sheet
AHV employer registration form
Suva risk tariff declaration and staff list
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late registrations are cured with retroactive effect from the incorporation date; default interest is applied to late VAT but penalties are waivable where the delay is attributable to registry timelines. Submit corrective filings immediately and request discretionary remission (Erlass) from the competent authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SHAB publication verification and operational cutover
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB) under the authority of the Federal Office for Buildings and Logistics, coordinated with the Commercial Register data hub Zefix.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 1-3 days after the register entry, verify the SHAB publication containing the company name, seat, capital, corporate purpose, registrants, and signature rules. Obtain certified extracts from Zefix/Commercial Register, activate the operational corporate bank account and payment rail integration for Apple App Store Payout and Google Play Payout, and install the registered office signage. This step constitutes the cutover point for executing commercial contracts and employment agreements.
required_dossiers: SHAB publication notice
Certified Zefix/Commercial Register extract
Registered office lease agreement or sublicense with the landlord
Operational bank onboarding forms including BIC/IBAN ledger identifiers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Material errors in SHAB or the register are cured by filing a rectification petition (Berichtigungsgesuch) with the Commercial Register Office; the corrected notice is republished at no material delay. Expedited entry at the registry stage accelerates the entire publication sequence.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - ISIC 5820 software publishing and MMORPG operation require no industrial or manufacturing permit under Swiss law; no cantonal industrial inspectorate (Gewerbeinspektorat) clearance is triggered for digital-only operations without a physical production facility.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating or manufacturing license required. Voluntary frameworks applicable to global MMORPG distribution: IARC/PEGI age-rating compliance, ISO/IEC 27001 information security certification, and Swiss-US Data Privacy Framework compliance under FDPIC supervision for personal data processing.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN; Bundesamt für Umwelt - BAFU)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - tertiary digital service category under the Swiss Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVPV/EIAO); no screening, scoping, or full EIA report is required for software publishing activities without physical installations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to production (zero manufacturing discharges). Residual duties: compliance with the Swiss Ordinance on Return, Take-Back and Disposal of Electrical and Electronic Equipment (ORD/VREG) for end-of-life servers and office IT hardware; municipal wastewater discharge thresholds under the Water Protection Ordinance (GSchV) for rented office premises; energy disclosure obligations under the CO2 Act for the occupied lease.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: certificate of compliance issued by the Cantonal Fire Police (Feuerpolizei Zug) covering the registered office premises; structural load clearance confirmed by the landlord for server racks and office equipment installations. Occupational safety: compliance with the Federal Labour Act (ArG), accident prevention directives of Suva/EKAS, mandatory UVG/LAA workplace accident insurance, and a documented workplace safety concept for all employees including remote Web3 developers.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC) via the official portal estv.admin.ch and the UID register (Zefix / UIDW).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity carrying out VAT-liable activities in Switzerland must register for VAT with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration through the online VAT registration form (Form / Formulaire 155.005) or via the Suisse Tax Portal (S-TP). The FTA issues a Swiss VAT number (MWST/Ust-ID) and a company identification number (UID/BE number). The registration process requires a business address, proof of identity of legal representatives, description of the planned Swiss activities, estimated turnover, and, where applicable, a Swiss customs declaration number. Advancement of registration before commencement is recommended; VAT liability is effective from the moment the turnover threshold is exceeded for supplies in Switzerland.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft (AG/SA) is a resident company subject to corporate income tax on worldwide income with tax residence based on registered office or place of effective management, and is jointly and severally liable for VAT as a taxable entity; non-resident companies without permanent establishment in Switzerland are only subject to Swiss tax on Swiss-source items, while VAT applies to supplies effected or deemed effected in Switzerland.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists in Switzerland. Available statutory elections include the election for VAT grouping (rowsing group for VAT purposes) among related Swiss entities, the election for corporate income tax grouping (Steuerkonsolidierung) at cantonal level, the election for deemed cost-plus / margin taxation for certain service activities, and the option to waive VAT exemption on real estate supplies. Hybrid mismatch rules under Swiss law (Art. 60a-60i of the Federal Act on Direct Federal Tax) provide defensive measures but no elective hybrid vehicle status.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / TVA) governed by the Federal Act on Value Added Tax (VAT Act, SR 641.20) and VAT Ordinance.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 of annual worldwide turnover from taxable supplies (irrespective of where customers are located), except that a lower CHF 150,000 threshold applies to subsidies and certain non-profit entities; foreign businesses that exceed CHF 100,000 of worldwide turnover become VAT-liable in Switzerland to the extent they perform supplies in Switzerland, including digital services to final consumers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland has no real-time fiscal clearance mandate and no compulsory government API clearance for standard B2B/B2C invoicing. E-invoicing in structured XML formats (e.g., Swiss eBill, QR-bill, EDI/XML) is recognized and encouraged; the Swiss QR-bill is mandatory for domestic invoices sent to private consumers for certain payment purposes and contains a unique QR reference. There is no nation-state digital stamping for VAT invoices; however, invoices must contain mandatory data per Art. 37 VAT Act (seller identification, UID number, invoice number, date, description, rate).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating applies to the export of tangible goods and to services provided in Switzerland when the service recipient is located abroad (based on the place-of-recipient rule or the place-of-benefit rule for services), provided the supplies are properly evidenced and the exporter keeps adequate books and records. For MMORPG digital supplies (e.g., in-app purchases, subscriptions, downloadable content), zero rating applies when the customer is a non-Swiss business or, for B2C digital services, the effective place of use and benefit is abroad and the supplier can demonstrate that the recipient resides outside Switzerland.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Swiss Customs Export Declaration / via NCTS or e-dec) and, for physical goods, a copy of the bill of lading or CIM consignment note / air waybill, together with a proof of departure from Switzerland.

Commercial invoice containing seller and buyer identification, description of exported goods or services, value, quantity, VAT zero-rating clause and reference to the export customs declaration number.

Inward Remittance Certificate or alternative banking settlement and SWIFT/IR evidence demonstrating that the export proceeds are received in accordance with the terms of the underlying contract, including proof of the customer's place of establishment for services.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Swiss tax authorities and the Federal Customs Administration may retrospectively audit export zero-rating within five years (extendable to ten years in cases of tax evasion). If zero rating is claimed without valid export documentation, the VAT is reclaimed at the standard rate equal to the input tax credit previously claimed, plus default interest (5% per annum) and a surcharge of up to 3 to 5 times the tax evaded in cases of fraudulent claims. Criminal liability can arise under Art. 184 VAT Act for tax evasion (Versteuerungsbetrug / fraude fiscale), with fines up to CHF 500,000 or imprisonment in severe cases. Additionally, the FTA can issue a penalty of 10% to 30% of the contested VAT for negligence, and a refusal to issue export certificates for future consignments.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB; Schweizerische Nationalbank, Banque Nationale Suisse, Banca Nazionale Svizzera)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland has accepted Article VIII obligations of the IMF; the Swiss franc is fully convertible on both current and capital account transactions. There are no exchange-control permits, no prior SNB approval for dividend distributions, profit remittances, principal repayments, or intra-group loans. The only practical restrictions are Swiss corporate law balance-sheet maintenance and the 35% Swiss withholding tax on dividends. No FX license is required for trade settlements or treasury operations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory export proceeds surrender or conversion ratio exists under Swiss law. Export receipts, including Apple App Store and Google Play payouts to the Swiss AG, may be retained in the original foreign currency (USD/EUR/GBP) in any Swiss bank account, or converted into CHF at the commercial market rate. The SNB requires statistical reporting in the aggregate by banks, but this does not impose a surrender, repatriation, or hedging obligation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Revenue Collection Account; segregated Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Constrained feasibility. An offshore digital EMI cannot act as the primary clearing house for the Swiss AG unless it is duly licensed by FINMA under the Swiss Payment Services Act (PSA) and is not merely serving Swiss customers through a cross-border digital channel. An EEA EMI may be used as an ancillary treasury/business wallet for platform receipts if the Swiss entity is the customer and the EMI does not conduct a payment business in Switzerland; primary corporate banking and settlement rails must remain with a Swiss licensed bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No absolute statutory requirement of physical presence for corporate account opening, but practical bank policy is stringent. Banks conduct AMLA-mandated identification of the AG, its directors, signatories, and beneficial owners. For a newly incorporated game-publishing AG with non-resident UBOs, at least one physical or authenticated audio-visual interview with a director is required by first-tier banks. Remote opening is not generally available prior to proof of commercial substance; local Swiss substance (registered office, general meeting place, tax compliance) materially shortens onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO chain and newly incorporated company with no audited financial history and limited Swiss substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial register extract (Handelsregisterauszug), articles of association and organization regulations, shareholder register and UBO declaration, passport and residence card of UBO, source-of-wealth statement and foreign tax filings, board resolution appointing a Swiss resident director, two-year business plan with revenue mix, signed Apple Developer Agreement and Google Play Developer Distribution Agreement, payment-flow diagram showing the AG as transaction counterparty only, and bank references from the UBO's home bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Massively multiplayer online in-app purchase volume from a global player base creates unexplained receivables and potential third-party settlement risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Monthly Apple/Google payout and commission statements, credit and debit reconciliation ledger, sanctions screening policy against OFAC/SECO/EU lists, IP geoblocking evidence excluding sanctioned territories, AML/CFT internal audit report, contractual representation that the AG does not custody player funds and is only a content seller under app-store terms.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Crypto/Web3 treasury exposure or expected conversion of gaming tokens for treasury purposes triggers high-risk digital-asset review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Proof of FINMA-licensed or equivalently regulated crypto exchange counterparty, zero-use of mixing/anonymity-enhancing tools, documented conversion policy with chain analytics report, segregation of game token accounts from corporate treasury, and board-approved treasury risk management framework.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Share capital increase is routed by SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA for EUR-denominated injections) directly to the AG's CHF-denominated operational account. Payment details must quote 'Share capital contribution — capital increase', the name of the shareholder, and the resolution date. The bank will hold funds after receipt until the updated commercial register excerpt confirms the capital increase; no SNB exchange-control approval is required. Verification pack includes signed capital increase resolution, subscribed and paid-in ledger, bank confirmation from originating bank, and board statement of deposit to the blocked capital account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for MMORPG development, licensing, and CDN services use SWIFT MT103 for direct payments; for large or documentary transactions confirmed irrevocable commercial letters of credit (MT700) are issued through a Swiss clearing bank. Cross-border vendor invoices are paid from the Swiss IBAN with bank reference to the underlying contract; no Swiss government dispatch is needed. CHF domestic clearing is executed through SIC/single Swiss interbank rails, while foreign-currency outflows settle through corresponding SWIFT correspondent accounts.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla foreign-exchange forwards (CHF versus USD, EUR, GBP; maturities up to 24 months) with FINMA-regulated Swiss banks or their counterparties
European-style foreign-exchange options and zero-cost collars
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (basis swaps) for balance-sheet asset/liability hedging
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) where the underlying currency is not deliverable or is restricted in the legal sense, provided the transaction complies with the issuing country's relevant rules

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting approval of annual financial statements, appropriation of net profit, and granting of discharge; signed minutes inserted in the corporate minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Meeting of Shareholders; no filing to the Commercial Register is required for a non-listed Swiss AG
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the balance-sheet date; the annual General Meeting must be held within this statutory period under Art. 699 CO
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No automatic administrative strike-off for a late AGM; directors remain exposed to liability and cannot invoke discharge, and a shareholder or creditor may obtain court-ordered measures or, in cases of manifest organizational defects, dissolution under Art. 731b CO.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory audit engagement: ordinary statutory audit or limited audit (review), or a valid shareholder resolution to opt out of audit where the 10-FTE exemption applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders at the ordinary Annual General Meeting; the auditor's report is retained with company books and is not publicly filed for a non-listed AG
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Auditor's report must be available before the AGM that adopts the annual financial statements; the AGM must be held within six months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A missing compulsory audit leaves the annual financial statements incomplete, deprives the board of valid discharge, creates civil liability for directors and auditors, and may be a ground for court-ordered corrective proceedings; it does not by itself trigger administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income and capital tax return covering Swiss federal direct tax, cantonal tax, and communal tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Authority of the canton of registered office; federal direct tax is also assessed through the cantonal administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the cantonally prescribed period, ordinarily four to six months after fiscal year-end; extensions are available upon written application
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing procedural fines of up to CHF 10,000, late-payment interest at approximately 4% per annum, summary assessment, and mandatory collection proceedings; unresolved insolvency may lead to bankruptcy and subsequent deletion from the Commercial Register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Register entries and corrections for actual events such as changes of registered office, share capital, directors, auditors, or branches; no annual commercial-register return is due
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Register Office of the canton of registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of the relevant event or resolution; no annual renewal or confirmation deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to register mandatory events is subject to administrative fines and third-party reliance liability; the company is not administratively struck off solely for missing an annual filing.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal corporate income tax rate calculated on profit after federal tax (equivalent to 7.83% effective federal rate on pre-tax profit); combined cantonal and communal effective rates typically range from 11% to 21%, with the Canton of Zug approximate all-in effective rate of 11.9%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Switzerland does not grant general statutory tax holidays. Cantonal innovation incentives include time-limited tax relief for newly established companies, R&D super-deductions in specific cantons, patent box regimes, and notional interest deduction on excess equity. An AG with substantial economic functions in Zug may elect ordinary taxation at competitive combined rates; holding, financing, mixed company, and domiciliary company privileges have been abolished for new entrants under OECD-compatible rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal and cantonal tax declaration for legal persons (''Steuererklärung juristische Personen'' / ''Formulaire personne morale''). Filing is made electronically through the cantonal e-filing portal, commonly TaxMe, or the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) eTax system for federal-level data.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The tax return must generally be filed within six months after the close of the fiscal year. Administrative extensions are available on request in most cantons, including Zug, but the final filing deadline is typically set by the cantonal tax authority and may not exceed each annual assessment cycle.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: AG legal name, commercial register number, date of incorporation, registered seat, board members and statutory representatives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide Swiss commercial register identification and precise beneficial ownership details. Non-resident directors must still be disclosed; absence of local substance must be explained to avoid anti-abuse review.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenues from MMORPG operations, in-app purchase sales, royalties, and licensing fees, less cost of sales, personnel, depreciation, amortization, and general operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use Swiss Accounting and Reporting Recommendations (Swiss GAAP FER) figures aligned with the commercial balance sheet. In-app revenues sourced through Apple App Store and Google Play must be recognized on gross or net basis per revenue recognition policy; consistency with transfer pricing documentation is mandatory.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered share capital, legal capital reserves, statutory reserves, and taxable equity components relevant to cantonal capital tax valuation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The minimum AG capital must remain CHF 100,000 fully subscribed and at least CHF 50,000 paid in. Non-resident shareholders must document shareholding percentages, acquisition costs, and any debt-financed equity contributions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of taxable dividend distributions, deemed distributions, and other movable capital income subject to Swiss federal withholding tax at 35%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all distributions made to non-resident shareholders. Failure to declare and remit withholding tax creates strict personal liability for directors. For profit repatriation under a tax treaty, the recipient must be identified as beneficial owner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible provisions, accrued liabilities, depreciation schedules, writedowns, and bad debt reserves.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure provisions respect commercial accounting standards and are not used as concealed profit reserves. Undocumented related-party provisions may be reclassified as constructive dividends subject to Swiss withholding tax and federal collection procedures.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts cantonal procedural fines and potential default assessments. Non-payment of assessed federal and cantonal corporate tax results in interest on arrears at approximately 4.5% per annum. Intentional false declarations may be prosecuted as tax evasion, subject to a fine up to three times the evaded tax; serious military-grade tax fraud is subject to additional criminal fines and, in aggravated cases, custodial penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% statutory Swiss federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) applies to dividend distributions and deemed distributions to shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident shareholder entitled to treaty benefits must submit a refund application using the official Swiss withholding tax refund form (Form 85) to the ESTV. The application must include a certificate of tax residence (TRC) from the shareholder's home tax authority, a declaration of beneficial ownership, and documentary evidence of the dividend payment. Upon approval, the excess withholding above the applicable treaty rate is refunded; typical treaty dividend rates for corporate shareholders holding 10%-25% capital range from 0% to 15%, depending on the relevant DTA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Switzerland does not impose domestic withholding tax on cross-border royalty payments for software licensing, MMORPG content licensing, or trademark licensing, resulting in a statutory rate of 0%. Interest paid on ordinary bank and intra-group loans is also not subject to Swiss withholding tax; however, interest on publicly issued bonds is subject to the 35% withholding tax. Most Swiss income tax treaties provide for royalty withholding rates of 0% and a 0% or 10% rate for interest, subject to beneficial ownership and anti-abuse limitation-of-benefits clauses.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Swiss tax law has no stand-alone statutory TP documentation threshold, but the ESTV requires contemporaneous OECD-compliant transfer pricing documentation when a Swiss company is part of an internationally active group and, as an administrative benchmark, when annual gross turnover exceeds CHF 80 million or cross-border related-party transactions are material. A Master File may be required for groups with consolidated global turnover of EUR 750 million or more under OECD BEPS-compliant practice; in any event, the taxpayer must bear the burden of proof for arm's length compliance.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland operates an entity-level taxation system with no general Economic Substance Regulations comparable to UAE ESR for ordinary operating AGs. However, substance requirements apply through tax treaty entitlement and anti-abuse rules: an MMORPG publishing AG must demonstrate real economic presence in Switzerland, including local strategic management, payroll, banking, and actual operational decision-making. In the absence of substance, passive royalty, dividend, and intercompany income can be recharacterized, denied treaty protection, subjected to Swiss withholding tax on deemed distributions, or classified as tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly filing false or incomplete tax returns, omitting Apple App Store or Google Play gross revenues, concealing foreign bank accounts, or artificially inflating deductible costs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax evaded is reclaimed with interest; administrative fine may reach up to three times the evaded tax; repeated or particularly serious evasion triggers criminal prosecution under the Swiss Federal Act on Direct Federal Tax and cantonal tax laws.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns or cause the AG to evade tax may be held personally liable for restitution of evaded tax and penalty amounts. Criminal conviction may include imprisonment for up to three years; serious cases involving forged records may lead to cross-border red notices and extradition proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Abuse of Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Swiss AG as a letterbox entity with no operational head office, no local personnel, no board meetings in Switzerland, and all substantive game publishing decisions made remotely abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax authorities may disregard the Swiss entity as fiscally nonexistent, allocate profits to the place of effective management, deny treaty relief on dividends and royalties, impose 35% withholding tax on deemed distributions, and levy penalty interest on underpaid taxes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly allow the company to operate without economic substance face public law liability for assessed taxes and withholding obligations. Travel bans may be imposed during international tax investigations, and personal bankruptcy proceedings may follow if the AG cannot satisfy tax debts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing payments from in-app purchases where funds are linked to fraudulent activity, laundering virtual currency proceeds, clearing third-party proceeds through the Swiss AG banking account without beneficial ownership verification, or accepting game-to-gold/value transfers used for money laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Willful money laundering under Article 305bis of the Swiss Criminal Code is punishable by imprisonment for up to three years; commercial or gang-related laundering carries imprisonment for up to five years plus fines. The Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA) may order asset freezes, and the AG may lose banking access.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are individually liable if they knew or should have known the source of funds was criminal. Personal sanctions include confiscation of assets, civil damages, and imprisonment. Non-resident directors remain subject to extradition from most jurisdictions for Swiss money laundering offenses.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Constructive Dividend and Hidden Profit Distribution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Entering into non-arm's-length agreements with a foreign related entity, e.g. overpaying for game publishing services or intellectual property licenses from a related shell company without economic justification, thereby shifting Swiss taxable profit abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Swiss tax authorities may recharacterize the excess payment as a tax-neutral but dividend-equivalent distribution subject to 35% withholding tax, add retroactive interest, reject deduction of the underlying expense, and impose penalty assessments of up to the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Board members who approve materially non-arm's-length transactions may face personal liability for withholding tax not collected, and for damages suffered by the AG. In severe cases involving intentional depletion of Swiss tax base, criminal sanctions for qualified tax evasion apply.
